record.original_question: Under reasonable growth conditions on W, determine whether global minimizers or suitably defined local minimizers y* of the elastic energy satisfy uniform positivity of the Jacobian determinant, namely whether there exists ε>0 such that det Dy*(x) ≥ ε for almost every x in Ω.

evidence.quote: det Dy∗ (x) ≥ ε for a.e. x ∈ Ω
Problem 6. Prove or disprove that, under reasonable growth conditions on W, global or suitably defined local minimizers of I satisfy (2.19).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2$ or $3$) be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary, representing the reference configuration of a hyperelastic body. Let $W: \Omega \times \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}_+ \to [0,\infty)$ be a stored-energy density, where $\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}_+ = \{F \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n} : \det F > 0\}$, satisfying:
(i) polyconvexity in $F$;
(ii) the standard coercivity/blow-up condition $W(x,F) \to \infty$ as $\det F \to 0^+$;
(iii) reasonable growth conditions from above (e.g., $W(x,F) \leq C(1+|F|^p+|\mathrm{cof}\,F|^q+(\det F)^r+(\det F)^{-s})$ for suitable exponents).

Consider the elastic energy
$$I(y) = \int_\Omega W(x, Dy(x))\,dx$$
defined on a class $\mathcal{A}$ of admissible deformations $y:\Omega \to \mathbb{R}^n$ in a Sobolev space (e.g., $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\det Dy > 0$ a.e.) subject to prescribed boundary conditions on (part of) $\partial\Omega$.

Problem. Prove or disprove: under such reasonable growth and coercivity hypotheses on $W$, every global minimizer (and, more generally, every suitably defined local minimizer) $y^*$ of $I$ over $\mathcal{A}$ satisfies the uniform positivity of the Jacobian
$$\exists\,\varepsilon > 0 \text{ such that } \det Dy^*(x) \geq \varepsilon \quad \text{for a.e. } x \in \Omega.$$
artifact.category_tag: Calculus of variations in nonlinear elasticity
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether minimizers of polyconvex elastic energies admit a uniform positive lower bound on the Jacobian determinant is a long-standing problem in nonlinear elasticity, originating in Ball's list of open problems. No general result establishing or refuting uniform positivity under broad reasonable growth conditions appears in the literature; only partial results in special settings (e.g., regularity under additional hypotheses, or near-identity deformations) are known. A direct web search returned no announcement of a resolution, so the problem appears to remain open.
